study.question: At the strongest fixed-angle negative-transfer model, which auxiliary task contributes consequential information to the transported orientation bit when transfer radius, line and support are retained from all tasks?
study.hypothesis: The joint auxiliary bit s(Q) can carry task-combination information beyond a generic coordinate sign. Omitting one task only from the computation of that bit may change the sign sequence and click AUC even though the injected transfer has the same line, radius and zero support at a common state. This is unverified, task attribution within the bit rather than whole-loss task utility.

nearest_work.difference: Exact-version archived primary text inspected at lines260-329: inherited unnormalized local activation and Dice only. The proposed task-specific surrogate VJP is not an original DIN component or exact DIN reproduction.
Keep the fixed-angle forward architecture and full-gradient radius/gates; replace only the sign bit by the same Q construction with one task cotangent zeroed for bit calculation.

Earlier subset trials changed the full auxiliary adapter-context transfer, including magnitude and direction. Here private task learning and full-task radius/geometry/gates remain, and only one bit source is ablated.

Authorized original text is unavailable (provenance only). Read the explicitly labeled UniRank fallback, which describes hub aggregation/broadcast, not this bit intervention. No gradient-method priority or originality claim is made; nearest gradient-method literature remains unverified.

DIN-derived unnormalized local activation and Dice; inherited compressed history/match-detail/task-product architecture
Four identity-edge cotangent collector, FP64 joint reduction and click-relative O
Fixed carriers, fixed pi/4 nuisance exclusion, full-task transported Q bit and inherited validity rules
True-label joint BCE, four heads, context-only auxiliary transfer and all existing detached paths
study.proposed_difference: Add bit-only leave-one-task-out constructions. For each task t in cart/fav/buy, keep ordered auxiliary cotangents but substitute zero for t solely while recomputing centered C_minus_t, O_minus_t, pair-reassigned/reprojected replacement and tangent Q_minus_t. Define its pivot bit by first maximal-absolute flattened coordinate, with exact zero -> +1. Replace s(Q_all) on the canonical full-task fixed-angle line by s(Q_minus_t). Keep external sign negative; do not recompute actual radius or output support from the omitted-task branch. Compute all new helpers in all four variants, including the unchanged all-task-bit bridge. No new parameters, buffers, RNG, forward labels or model passes.
predictions: At common state every intervention differs from bridge only by a batch-global +/- sign on active transfer; FP64 Frobenius norm, canonical line, occupied zero rows and full-task zero support match.

If one task contributes useful information through this bit, its omission produces bit disagreements and lower validation click AUC versus the all-task-bit bridge. If omission improves AUC, that task has harmful influence through this bit in this setting.
If bit omission rarely changes s(Q), similar outcomes are expected and are a weak intervention rather than evidence of task irrelevance.
Forward capacity and inference work remain unchanged. Training gets three additional context-sized projection/bit computations in every cell; measure rather than claim equal wall cost.
falsifiers: If all task omissions frequently change bits but do not reproducibly change AUC, the hypothesis of consequential per-task bit information lacks support at this fixed external sign.
Differences in same-state forward probabilities, Dice state, private gradients, output norm/support or bridge replay invalidate isolated bit attribution.
A small single-seed AUC difference alone does not establish a mechanism; bootstrap/paired-seed uncertainty or a sign-factorial follow-up may overturn it.
No result here establishes all auxiliary supervision is useful: full-task radius/gates/history/private learning remain and the custom backward is not the derivative of joint BCE.
alternative_explanations: Coordinate pivot/tie sensitivity, FP64-to-input-dtype casting, repeated-ID scatter and adaptive optimizer can turn arbitrary sign changes into trajectory differences.
The reduced Q uses its own bit degeneracy and zero -> +1 convention; sign changes could reflect numerical degeneracy or generic sign frequency rather than semantic task information.
Full-task auxiliary radius and inherited gate still contain every task; later model states diverge, so this is not removal of a task label or its total causal effect.

External sign interaction is plausible from g3-r0059 and g3-r0060; this round intentionally fixes the better negative sign. A consequential result requires a subsequent paired sign-factorial and repetition.
Extensive adaptive validation search and one training seed create selection bias; deterministic same-seed bridges are implementation controls, not independent replication.
Earlier g3-r0039 replay and g3-r0041 reduction discrepancies show sensitivity to collection/precision; retain FP64 and reject unmatched bridges rather than pool those observations.
